Every NAEP release produces league tables of states. But NAEP tests a *sample* of
students in each state, so every score carries sampling error, and many of the gaps
between neighboring states in a ranking are too small to distinguish from chance.
This page redraws the 2024 state results using the significance tests published by
the National Center for Education Statistics (NCES), such that the magnitude of the
differences is easy to spot.

Select a jurisdiction, a subject, and grade:

```{r}
#| label: data
#| echo: true
library(dplyr)
library(readr)

estimates  <- read_csv("data/estimates.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
state_tests <- read_csv("data/state_comparisons.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
year_tests  <- read_csv("data/year_comparisons.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
latest <- max(estimates$year)

# Ranking: A jurisdiction's raw rank orders the unrounded averages.
# Its rank range counts only significant differences: it cannot rank
# better than one place below everyone who scored significantly higher,
# or worse than one place above everyone who scored significantly lower.
standing <- state_tests |>
  filter(focal != "NP", other != "NP") |>
  summarize(
    n_higher = sum(result == "lower"),    # others that scored higher than focal
    n_same   = sum(result == "equal"),
    n_lower  = sum(result == "higher"),
    .by = c(subject, grade, focal)
  ) |>
  rename(code = focal) |>
  inner_join(
    estimates |> filter(year == latest, code != "NP") |> select(subject, grade, code, mean),
    by = c("subject", "grade", "code")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    n = n(),
    raw_rank = min_rank(desc(mean)),
    best_rank = 1 + n_higher,
    worst_rank = n - n_lower,
    .by = c(subject, grade)
  )

ojs_define(
  estimates_cols = estimates, state_tests_cols = state_tests,
  year_tests_cols = year_tests, standing_cols = standing, latest = latest
)
```

```{ojs}
est = transpose(estimates_cols)
stateTests = transpose(state_tests_cols)
yearTests = transpose(year_tests_cols)
standing = transpose(standing_cols)

HIGHER = "#1c5cab"
LOWER = "#c2501c"
SAME = "#dddcd7"
INK = "#0b0b0b"
MUTED = "#52514e"
GRID = "#e6e5e1"
NATION = "NP"
W = 720

jurisdictions = Array.from(d3.group(est.filter(d => d.code !== NATION), d => d.code), ([code, rows]) => ({code, jurisdiction: rows[0].jurisdiction}))
  .sort((a, b) => d3.ascending(a.jurisdiction, b.jurisdiction))
```

::: {.controls}

```{ojs}
viewof focal = Inputs.select(jurisdictions, {label: "Jurisdiction", format: d => d.jurisdiction, value: jurisdictions.find(d => d.code === "MD")})
viewof subject = Inputs.radio(["Mathematics", "Reading"], {label: "Subject", value: "Mathematics"})
viewof grade = Inputs.radio([4, 8], {label: "Grade", value: 8, format: d => `Grade ${d}`})
```

:::

```{ojs}
// current selection 
name = focal.jurisdiction
cur = est.filter(d => d.subject === subject && d.grade === grade)
now = cur.filter(d => d.year === latest)
me = now.find(d => d.code === focal.code)
nation = now.find(d => d.code === NATION)
rank = standing.find(d => d.subject === subject && d.grade === grade && d.code === focal.code)
tests = new Map(stateTests.filter(d => d.subject === subject && d.grade === grade && d.focal === focal.code).map(d => [d.other, d]))
overTime = yearTests.filter(d => d.subject === subject && d.grade === grade)
label = `grade ${grade} ${subject.toLowerCase()}`

// small functions
ordinal = n => n + (["th", "st", "nd", "rd"][(n % 100 >> 3 ^ 1) && n % 10] || "th")
signed = x => (Math.round(x) > 0 ? "+" : Math.round(x) < 0 ? "−" : "") + Math.abs(Math.round(x))
count = (n, word) => `${n} ${word}${n === 1 ? "" : "s"}`
points = x => count(Math.abs(Math.round(x)), "point")
textOn = fill => fill === SAME || fill === "#fff" ? INK : "#fff"

// Tile-grid layout: one equal-sized tile per jurisdiction, so small states and
// DC are as readable as large ones.
tiles = new Map(Object.entries({
  AK: [0, 0], ME: [0, 11],
  VT: [1, 10], NH: [1, 11],
  WA: [2, 1], ID: [2, 2], MT: [2, 3], ND: [2, 4], MN: [2, 5], IL: [2, 6], WI: [2, 7], MI: [2, 8], NY: [2, 9], RI: [2, 10], MA: [2, 11],
  OR: [3, 1], NV: [3, 2], WY: [3, 3], SD: [3, 4], IA: [3, 5], IN: [3, 6], OH: [3, 7], PA: [3, 8], NJ: [3, 9], CT: [3, 10],
  CA: [4, 1], UT: [4, 2], CO: [4, 3], NE: [4, 4], MO: [4, 5], KY: [4, 6], WV: [4, 7], VA: [4, 8], MD: [4, 9], DE: [4, 10],
  AZ: [5, 2], NM: [5, 3], KS: [5, 4], AR: [5, 5], TN: [5, 6], NC: [5, 7], SC: [5, 8], DC: [5, 9],
  OK: [6, 4], LA: [6, 5], MS: [6, 6], AL: [6, 7], GA: [6, 8],
  HI: [7, 0], TX: [7, 4], FL: [7, 9], DS: [7, 11]
}))

// rows: [{code, fill, value, tip, focal}]
tileMap = rows => Plot.plot({
  width: W, height: 8 * 52, margin: 2,
  x: {type: "band", domain: d3.range(12), axis: null, padding: 0.07},
  y: {type: "band", domain: d3.range(8), axis: null, padding: 0.07},
  marks: [
    Plot.cell(rows, {x: d => tiles.get(d.code)[1], y: d => tiles.get(d.code)[0], fill: "fill", rx: 5,
      stroke: d => d.focal ? INK : "none", strokeWidth: 2.5, title: "tip", tip: true}),
    Plot.text(rows, {x: d => tiles.get(d.code)[1], y: d => tiles.get(d.code)[0], text: d => d.code === "DS" ? "DoD" : d.code,
      dy: -7, fontSize: 12.5, fontWeight: 600, fill: d => textOn(d.fill), pointerEvents: "none"}),
    Plot.text(rows, {x: d => tiles.get(d.code)[1], y: d => tiles.get(d.code)[0], text: "value",
      dy: 9, fontSize: 11.5, fill: d => textOn(d.fill), pointerEvents: "none"})
  ]
})

key = items => html`<div class="key">${items.map(([cls, style, text]) => html`<span><span class="swatch ${cls}" style="${style}"></span>${text}</span>`)}</div>`
```

## Where does it really stand?

```{ojs}
md`In ${latest}, **${name}**'s average ${label} score was **${Math.round(me.mean)}**. By raw score that is
**${ordinal(rank.raw_rank)} of ${rank.n}** jurisdictions. But ${count(rank.n_same, "jurisdiction")} had
${rank.n_same === 1 ? "a score" : "scores"} that NCES found *not significantly different* from ${name}'s.
Only ${rank.n_higher} scored significantly higher and ${rank.n_lower} significantly lower. Counting only those
differences, ${name} sits somewhere between **${ordinal(rank.best_rank)}** and **${ordinal(rank.worst_rank)}**.`
```

```{ojs}
vsNation = tests.get(NATION)
html`<div class="tiles">
  <div class="tile"><div class="tile-label">Average score, ${latest}</div><div class="tile-value">${Math.round(me.mean)}</div>
    <div class="tile-detail">National public ${Math.round(nation.mean)}: ${name} is ${vsNation.result === "equal" ? "not significantly different" : `significantly ${vsNation.result}`}</div></div>
  <div class="tile"><div class="tile-label">Raw rank</div><div class="tile-value">${ordinal(rank.raw_rank)}</div>
    <div class="tile-detail">of ${rank.n} jurisdictions</div></div>
  <div class="tile"><div class="tile-label">Rank range</div><div class="tile-value">${rank.best_rank}–${rank.worst_rank}</div>
    <div class="tile-detail">counting significant differences only</div></div>
  <div class="tile"><div class="tile-label">Statistical ties</div><div class="tile-value">${rank.n_same}</div>
    <div class="tile-detail">jurisdictions not significantly different</div></div>
</div>`
```

### Every jurisdiction, compared with the selected one

```{ojs}
// result describes the focal jurisdiction relative to the other one, so a
// "lower" result means the other jurisdiction scored higher.
compared = now.filter(d => d.code !== NATION).map(d => {
  const isFocal = d.code === focal.code
  const t = tests.get(d.code)
  const status = isFocal ? "focal" : !t ? "none" : t.result === "lower" ? "higher" : t.result === "higher" ? "lower" : "same"
  const diff = d.mean - me.mean
  const fill = {focal: "#fff", higher: HIGHER, lower: LOWER, same: SAME, none: "#f4f4f2"}[status]
  const verdict = {focal: "Selected jurisdiction", higher: `Significantly higher than ${name}`, lower: `Significantly lower than ${name}`,
    same: `Not significantly different from ${name}`, none: "No test available"}[status]
  return {...d, focal: isFocal, status, diff, fill, verdict, value: isFocal ? Math.round(d.mean) : signed(diff),
    tip: `${d.jurisdiction}\nAverage score ${Math.round(d.mean)}${isFocal ? "" : ` (${signed(diff)} vs ${name})`}\n${verdict}`}
})

key([
  ["ring", "", `${name} (average score shown)`],
  ["", `background:${HIGHER}`, "Scored significantly higher"],
  ["", `background:${SAME}`, "Not significantly different"],
  ["", `background:${LOWER}`, "Scored significantly lower"]
])
```

```{ojs}
tileMap(compared)
```

::: {.note}
Numbers are each jurisdiction's average score minus the selected jurisdiction's, in scale points. DoD is the Department of Defense school system (DoDEA).
:::

### The ranking, with the ties marked

```{ojs}
ranked = d3.sort(compared, d => -d.mean)

Plot.plot({
  width: W, height: ranked.length * 17 + 50, marginLeft: 150, marginRight: 30, marginTop: 28,
  x: {label: null, grid: true, nice: true, axis: "top"},
  y: {label: null, domain: ranked.map(d => d.jurisdiction), tickSize: 0},
  marks: [
    Plot.ruleY([name], {stroke: "#eaf1fb", strokeWidth: 15}),
    Plot.ruleX([nation.mean], {stroke: MUTED, strokeDasharray: "3,3"}),
    Plot.text([nation], {x: "mean", frameAnchor: "bottom", dy: 14, text: d => `National public ${Math.round(d.mean)}`, fill: MUTED, fontSize: 11}),
    Plot.dot(ranked, {x: "mean", y: "jurisdiction", r: 5.5, fill: "fill", stroke: d => d.focal ? INK : d.status === "same" ? "#8a8984" : "#fff",
      strokeWidth: d => d.focal ? 2.5 : 1, title: "tip", tip: true})
  ]
})
```

::: {.note}
Average scale score, 2024, highest first. Same colors as the map: gray dots are statistical ties with the selected jurisdiction, wherever they fall in the order.
:::

## Has it recovered since 2019?

```{ojs}
myTrend = cur.filter(d => d.code === focal.code)
usTrend = cur.filter(d => d.code === NATION)
myYearTests = new Map(overTime.filter(d => d.code === focal.code && d.stat === "mean").map(d => [d.earlier_year, d]))
since19 = myYearTests.get(2019)
since22 = myYearTests.get(2022)
describe = t => !t ? "cannot be compared" : t.result === "equal" ? "not significantly different" : `significantly ${t.result} (${signed(t.gap)} points)`

md`Compared with 2019, the last assessment before the pandemic, ${name}'s ${latest} score is **${describe(since19)}**.
Compared with 2022 it is **${describe(since22)}**.`
```

```{ojs}
key([
  ["", `background:${HIGHER}; border-radius:50%`, `${name}: significantly different from ${latest}`],
  ["", `background:#fff; border:2.5px solid ${HIGHER}; border-radius:50%`, `${name}: not significantly different from ${latest}`],
  ["", `background:#8a8984; height:3px; vertical-align:4px`, "National public"]
])
```

```{ojs}
Plot.plot({
  width: W, height: 320, marginLeft: 46, marginRight: 20,
  x: {label: null, ticks: usTrend.map(d => d.year), tickFormat: "d"},
  y: {label: "Average scale score", grid: true, nice: true},
  marks: [
    Plot.lineY(usTrend, {x: "year", y: "mean", stroke: "#8a8984", strokeWidth: 2}),
    Plot.lineY(myTrend, {x: "year", y: "mean", stroke: HIGHER, strokeWidth: 2.5}),
    Plot.dot(myTrend, {x: "year", y: "mean", r: 5, stroke: HIGHER, strokeWidth: 2.5,
      fill: d => d.year === latest || myYearTests.get(d.year)?.result !== "equal" ? HIGHER : "#fff"}),
    Plot.ruleX(usTrend, Plot.pointerX({x: "year", stroke: MUTED, strokeOpacity: 0.5})),
    Plot.tip(myTrend, Plot.pointerX({x: "year", y: "mean", title: d => {
      const t = myYearTests.get(d.year), us = usTrend.find(u => u.year === d.year)
      return `${d.year}\n${name}: ${Math.round(d.mean)}\nNational public: ${us ? Math.round(us.mean) : "n/a"}` +
        (d.year === latest ? "" : `\n${latest} is ${describe(t)} relative to ${d.year}`)
    }}))
  ]
})
```

### The same test in every jurisdiction

```{ojs}
change = now.map(d => {
  const t = overTime.find(t => t.code === d.code && t.stat === "mean" && t.earlier_year === 2019)
  const status = !t ? "none" : t.result
  const fill = {lower: LOWER, higher: HIGHER, equal: SAME, none: "#f4f4f2"}[status]
  const verdict = {lower: "Significantly lower than in 2019", higher: "Significantly higher than in 2019",
    equal: "Not significantly different from 2019", none: "No test available"}[status]
  return {...d, status, fill, focal: d.code === focal.code, value: t ? signed(t.gap) : "",
    tip: `${d.jurisdiction}\n${latest} score ${Math.round(d.mean)}${t ? ` (${signed(t.gap)} since 2019)` : ""}\n${verdict}`}
})
changeStates = change.filter(d => d.code !== NATION)
tally = d3.rollup(changeStates, v => v.length, d => d.status)

md`Across the ${changeStates.length} jurisdictions, **${tally.get("lower") ?? 0}** scored significantly lower in ${latest} than in 2019,
**${tally.get("equal") ?? 0}** were not significantly different, and **${tally.get("higher") ?? 0}** scored significantly higher.`
```

```{ojs}
key([
  ["", `background:${LOWER}`, "Significantly lower than 2019"],
  ["", `background:${SAME}`, "Not significantly different"],
  ["", `background:${HIGHER}`, "Significantly higher than 2019"],
  ["ring", "", name]
])
```

```{ojs}
tileMap(changeStates)
```

::: {.note}
Numbers are the change in average score from 2019 to 2024, in scale points.
:::

## Who lost ground?

An average can hide a widening spread. NAEP also reports the scores at the 10th, 25th,
50th, 75th, and 90th percentiles, which show whether lower- and higher-performing
students moved together.

```{ojs}
PCT = [["p90", "90th percentile"], ["p75", "75th"], ["p50", "50th (median)"], ["p25", "25th"], ["p10", "10th percentile"]]
pctChange = [focal.code, NATION].flatMap(code => PCT.map(([stat, lab]) => {
  const t = overTime.find(t => t.code === code && t.stat === stat && t.earlier_year === 2019)
  return t && {who: code === NATION ? "National public" : name, isFocal: code !== NATION, stat, lab, gap: t.gap, sig: t.result !== "equal"}
})).filter(d => d)
mine = new Map(pctChange.filter(d => d.isFocal).map(d => [d.stat, d]))
lo = mine.get("p10")
hi = mine.get("p90")
say = d => `${d.gap < 0 ? "fell" : "rose"} ${points(d.gap)}${d.sig ? "" : " (not a significant change)"}`

lo && hi
  ? md`In ${name}, the score at the **10th percentile ${say(lo)}** between 2019 and ${latest}, and the score at the
**90th percentile ${say(hi)}**. ${Math.round(lo.gap) < Math.round(hi.gap) ? "Lower-performing students lost more ground than higher-performing students." : Math.round(lo.gap) > Math.round(hi.gap) ? "Higher-performing students lost more ground, or gained less, than lower-performing students." : "The two ends of the distribution moved by the same amount."}`
  : md`Percentile comparisons are not available for this selection.`
```

```{ojs}
key([
  ["", `background:${HIGHER}; border-radius:50%`, `${name}: significant change`],
  ["", `background:#fff; border:2.5px solid ${HIGHER}; border-radius:50%`, `${name}: not significant`],
  ["", `background:#8a8984; border-radius:50%`, "National public: significant change"],
  ["", `background:#fff; border:2.5px solid #8a8984; border-radius:50%`, "National public: not significant"]
])
```

```{ojs}
Plot.plot({
  width: W, height: 320, marginLeft: 120, marginRight: 30, marginBottom: 46,
  x: {label: `Change in score, 2019 to ${latest} (scale points)`, labelOffset: 40, grid: true, nice: true},
  y: {label: null, domain: PCT.map(d => d[1]), tickSize: 0},
  fy: {label: null},
  marks: [
    Plot.ruleX([0], {stroke: INK}),
    ...[true, false].map(isFocal => Plot.dot(pctChange.filter(d => d.isFocal === isFocal), {x: "gap", y: "lab", r: 6, strokeWidth: 2.5,
      dy: isFocal ? -7 : 7,
      stroke: isFocal ? HIGHER : "#8a8984",
      fill: d => !d.sig ? "#fff" : isFocal ? HIGHER : "#8a8984",
      title: d => `${d.who}\n${d.lab}: ${signed(d.gap)} points\n${d.sig ? "Significant change" : "Not a significant change"}`, tip: true}))
  ]
})
```

### The whole distribution since 2003

```{ojs}
fan = myTrend.flatMap(d => PCT.map(([stat, lab]) => ({year: d.year, stat, lab: lab.replace(" percentile", "").replace(" (median)", ""), score: d[stat]}))).filter(d => d.score != null)

Plot.plot({
  width: W, height: 340, marginLeft: 46, marginRight: 48,
  x: {label: null, ticks: usTrend.map(d => d.year), tickFormat: "d"},
  y: {label: `${name}: score at each percentile`, grid: true, nice: true},
  marks: [
    Plot.lineY(fan, {x: "year", y: "score", z: "stat", stroke: HIGHER, strokeWidth: d => d.stat === "p50" ? 2.5 : 1.5}),
    Plot.text(fan, Plot.selectLast({x: "year", y: "score", z: "stat", text: "lab", textAnchor: "start", dx: 6, fill: INK, fontSize: 11})),
    Plot.dot(fan, Plot.pointer({x: "year", y: "score", r: 4, fill: HIGHER, stroke: "#fff",
      title: d => `${d.year}\n${d.lab} percentile: ${Math.round(d.score)}`, tip: true}))
  ]
})
```

## The comparison as a table

```{ojs}
Inputs.table(ranked.map((d, i) => ({
  "Raw rank": i + 1,
  Jurisdiction: d.jurisdiction,
  "Average score": Math.round(d.mean),
  [`Difference from ${name}`]: d.focal ? "" : signed(d.diff),
  "NCES test": d.verdict
})), {rows: 14, layout: "auto"})
```

## Data and method

**Source.** National Assessment of Educational Progress (NAEP), mathematics and reading,
grades 4 and 8, 2003 to 2024, public schools. Estimates and significance tests come from the
[NAEP Data Service API](https://www.nationsreportcard.gov/api_endpoint.aspx) of the National
Center for Education Statistics. `scripts/fetch_naep.R` rebuilds the data files.

**Significance tests.** Every "significantly higher", "lower", or "not significantly different"
on this page is NCES's own determination, as returned by the API. Nothing is re-estimated here.
The API does not publish standard errors, so this page shows no confidence intervals and does not
approximate any. "Not significantly different" means the data cannot distinguish the two scores.
It does not mean they are equal.

**Rank range.** The raw rank orders the unrounded average scores of the 52 jurisdictions (50
states, the District of Columbia, and DoDEA). The rank range is derived here from NCES's pairwise
tests: the best rank is one more than the number of jurisdictions that scored significantly
higher, and the worst rank is 52 minus the number that scored significantly lower. It is a
summary of the pairwise results, not a formal confidence interval for the rank.

**Limits.**

- Each test is a single pairwise comparison.
- "Not significantly different" is not transitive: A can tie with B, and B with C, while A and C differ.
- Scores are shown rounded to whole points, as NAEP reports them. Ranks and tests use unrounded values.
- Statistical significance is not educational significance. A small difference can be significant in a large state.
